name: SAVE
fullName: Sleep Apnea Cardiovascular Endpoints — CPAP for Prevention of Cardiovascular Events in Obstructive Sleep Apnea (SAVE)
population: n=2717, 45-75 years; most participants were men, NIHSS not reported — enrolment was by established coronary or cerebrovascular disease, not stroke severity, mean follow-up 3.7 years
finding: DID NOT meet: a primary end-point event occurred in 229 CPAP participants (17.0%) and 207 usual-care participants (15.4%) — the point estimate favors usual care
teachingPoint: Teaches that CPAP should be offered for symptoms — sleepiness, snoring, quality of life — and not promised as a way to prevent recurrent vascular events; the largest randomized test found no event reduction.

name: Post-stroke PAP meta-analysis
fullName: Post-stroke sleep disordered breathing and the effect of positive airway pressure treatment: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
population: n=1457, not reported in the abstract, NIHSS not reported in the abstract, records searched from inception in July 2024 up to September 2024; 72,387 records screened
teachingPoint: Keeps the post-stroke sleep-apnea question open rather than closing it: a pooled signal for fewer recurrent vascular events sits against a larger neutral trial, and neither supports promising a patient that PAP will improve functional independence.
